The 30-year-old is in his third season with Montreal after being acquired early in the 2024-25 campaign. Carrier is averaging 20:35 per night so far in the early going as he has been pressed into consistent top-four duty with Mike Matheson and Kaiden Guhle dealing with injuries at times this season. He also has seven points in 22 games, matching his point-per-game pace from a year ago. Carrier is carrying a $3.75MM and as a right-shot defender (the side that’s highly coveted), he’s in line to land a nice raise on his next deal. AFP Analytics projects that he could land around $5MM on a short-term agreement next summer, a price tag that might be deemed too expensive by Montreal, especially if prospect David Reinbacher shows he’s NHL-ready by then.

items.title: Canucks’ Elias Pettersson out with upper-body injury
items.summary: The Vancouver Canucks are looking for just their second home win in 11 games this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vancouver Canucks will be without star center Elias Pettersson on Saturday night as they host the Minnesota Wild at Rogers Arena, and the game could also go ahead without former captain Quinn Hughes on the visiting blueline. The Canucks confirmed that Pettersson will miss Saturday’s matchup with an upper-body injury, though it is unclear when it occurred, as the Swedish forward played over 22 minutes in Thursday’s 5-1 loss to the Seattle Kraken . Sitting second in team scoring with six goals and 17 assists for 23 points, the now-28-year-old has enjoyed a bounce-back season so far, after scoring just 15 goals and 51 points in 74 games in 2025-26. Outside of his increased offensive contributions, he also has the most shot blocks among all NHL forwards this season, with 32 blocks over 24 games. Vancouver comes into Saturday’s matchup, the first of a back-to-back set, seeking just a second win on home ice in their 11th home game, after a road trip that saw them pick up rare consecutive wins against the Vegas Golden Knights and Utah Mammoth , before falling to the Kraken. It will also mark the second time Hughes is scheduled to return to Rogers Arena after the Canucks traded him to the Wild in a blockbuster deal 11 months ago. While Hughes had to leave Minnesota’s last game against the Calgary Flames , there were no updates on his condition as of Saturday morning. Once the final buzzer sounds between the Canucks and Wild, Vancouver will turn its attention to a Sunday clash with the Chicago Blackhawks , which won’t feature Blackhawks star center and North Vancouver native Connor Bedard due to a shoulder injury suffered while taking a faceoff earlier in the week against the Toronto Maple Leafs .

items.title: Blue Jackets’ Matthew Knies says return to Toronto ‘feels a little awkward’
items.summary: Knies is set to make his first start at Scotiabank Arena since the trade prior to the start of the 2026-27 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matthew Knies never expected to be traded by the Toronto Maple Leafs . And then, a day before Toronto’s first game of the season, he was shipped out to the Columbus Blue Jackets in a deal that sent Kirill Marchenko the other way. Now, Knies is back at Scotiabank Arena for the first time since the deal. Knies was selected 57th overall in 2021 by Toronto, and went on to score 72 goals and 172 points in 260 games over five years with the club. The 2026-27 season has been a bit of a struggle for both Knies and the Blue Jackets, who enter Saturday’s bout sitting in 29th place – and in a tie with Pittsburgh for last in the Eastern Conference. The Leafs themselves have struggled this year, with the club going 1-8-1 over the past 10 games. Toronto currently sits 27th in the NHL with just 19 points, three ahead of the Blue Jackets. Still, Knies is making the most of the new opportunity, which all came together quickly after thinking he’d spend the year in Toronto. “I didn’t think about [the possibility of a trade] at all,” Knies told reporters on Saturday. “I never thought it would really happen, so that’s just the confidence I had that, you know, I needed to play on this team. items.summary: Dakota Mermis will fill in for OEL on the Maple Leafs’ third pairing against Columbus.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller confirmed that the team will make veteran defenseman Oliver Ekman-Larsson a healthy scratch for their game against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday. Ekman-Larsson, 35, has recorded just one point (an assist) while averaging 18:31 of ice time across 24 games with the Maple Leafs this season. Hiller confirmed that Dakota Mermis will take Ekman-Larsson’s place on the left side of the Leafs’ third pairing with Troy Stecher. The Leafs have lost eight consecutive games heading into their matchup with the Blue Jackets at Scotiabank Arena on Saturday. The two teams are scheduled to hit the ice in Toronto at 7:00 p.m. Eastern. Ekman-Larsson is currently in the third season of the four-year contract he signed with the Maple Leafs as an unrestricted free agent in 2024. The 6’2″ left-shot defenseman is signed through 2028 at a $3.5 million annual cap hit. A holdover from the previous iteration of the Leafs, which were managed by Brad Treliving and coached by Craig Berube, Ekman-Larsson’s future in Toronto increasingly looks unclear under Hiller and new GM John Chayka. His contract includes a 16-team no-trade list for both the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons. The Phoenix Coyotes originally selected Ekman-Larsson in the first round (No. 6 overall) of the 2009 NHL Draft. The smooth-skating Swede spent the first 11 seasons of his NHL career in Arizona, most notably helping the Coyotes reach the 2012 Western Conference Final, before being traded to the Vancouver Canucks in 2021. After two disappointing seasons in Vancouver, Ekman-Larsson was bought out of his contract and allowed to sign with the Florida Panthers , with whom he spent one year and won the Stanley Cup in 2024. items.summary: The New York Rangers will be placing center Luke Glendening on waivers on Saturday.
items.body: Register Login Rangers Place Luke Glendening On Waivers By Brian La Rose | at November 21, 2026 11:50 am After adding a center on Friday in Max Sasson , the Rangers will be parting ways with another one. Peter Baugh of The Athletic relays ( Twitter link ) that New York will be placing veteran middleman Luke Glendening on waivers today at 1 PM CT when the waiver period opens up. The 37-year-old was without a team to start the season. He spent training camp in Tampa Bay on a PTO deal but didn’t secure a full contract with them. However, just past the midway mark of October, he secured a PTO with the Rangers on the heels of Joe Veleno ’s long-term injury. A few days later, he was converted to a one-year, $850K contract. Glendening hasn’t played a lot on that deal, however, as he has made just four appearances since being signed; just two of those have come this month. He’s still looking for his first point of the season but has won over 71% of his draws in his limited action. For the past several seasons, Glendening has had a very limited role wherever he has played. He’s a capable penalty killer and a faceoff specialist but typically provides very little offensive production; he has only reached double-digit points once since the 2021-22 season, that being an 11-point effort. For his career, Glendening has 175 points in 938 games over parts of 14 NHL seasons with six different organizations. Given that he was claimed off waivers last season at the trade deadline, it’s not a given that Glendening will pass through unclaimed this time. While he has a very niche role to fill, if a team needs some help at the faceoff dot or on the penalty kill, they could be inclined to take a low-cost flyer on Glendening’s services. items.summary: Brendan Gallagher has been placed on the injured reserve with a lower-body injury, and forwards Ty Mueller and Jacob Quillan and goaltender Nikita Tolopilo have been recalled from the American Hockey League, the team announced Saturday.
items.body: The Vancouver Canucks are juggling their roster ahead of a back-to-back this weekend. Brendan Gallagher has been placed on the injured reserve with a lower-body injury, and forwards Ty Mueller and Jacob Quillan and goaltender Nikita Tolopilo have been recalled from the American Hockey League, the team announced Saturday. Gallagher's placement on the IR is retroactive to Nov. 19, when he suffered the injury in a 5-1 loss to the Seattle Kraken. He took an awkward fall after getting tangled up in front of the net and left the game in obvious discomfort at 11:30 in the second period, with Vancouver down 3-1. Gallagher has three points in 20 games this season for the Canucks. Meanwhile, Mueller will be in line for his first taste of NHL action this season, should he lace up for the Canucks. He's spent the year with AHL Abbotsford and has seven goals and five assists in 17 games. The 23-year-old was drafted by the Canucks in the fourth round in 2023 and has one goal in eight appearances at the NHL level in the prior two seasons. Quillan, 24, last suited up for Vancouver on Nov. 5, recording his first and only point with the team in three games this year. He has five goals and two assists in seven games with Abbotsford. Tolopilo, 26, played well in his lone appearance for the Canucks this year, a 3-2 win over the Utah Mammoth on Nov. 16. Over his three seasons in the NHL, he has a 3.44 goals-against average and .885 save percentage in 24 games played (20 starts). The Canucks will take on the Minnesota Wild on Saturday Night Hockey, with puck drop at 10 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. PCT on Sportsnet and Sportsnet+. They follow it up with a game against the Chicago Blackhawks Sunday night at 8 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. PCT.

items.title: Line brawl breaks out between Michigan, Michigan State
items.body: There is no love lost between the University of Michigan and Michigan State hockey teams. A line brawl broke out on Friday night between the intra-state rivals — a rarity in college hockey, where the NCAA strictly prohibits fighting across all sports, including hockey. The melee started when Michigan State defenceman Sean Barnhill laid a hit from behind on Michigan forward and Toronto Maple Leafs prospect Nick Moldenhauer. Multiple fights ensued with members of the Michigan State penalty box skating out to join in on the fracas. In total, a combined 71 penalty minutes were handed out, including five major penalties and four disqualifications. Per the NCAA prohibition on fighting, a disqualification results in an automatic one-game suspension. Players facing the ban include Barnhill, Nick Sima, Drew Shock and Montreal Canadiens prospect Michael Hage. Time will tell if a rematch is in order or if cooler heads will prevail, as the two teams face each other again on Saturday night.

items.body: Teammates cheer on forward in AHL rehab assignment in recovery from hip surgery BROSSARD, Quebec -- Jonathan Huberdeau received the best possible show of affection for his return to hockey on Wednesday after having a left hip resurfacing operation in March. items.body: CALGARY — There aren't many equipment managers who get to celebrate a highlight-reel assist, get a shoutout on Sportsnet and have an NHL defenceman searching for a fine bottle of wine for them. Ben Dumaine managed all three Thursday night, thanks to a quick reaction that helped Simon Nemec turn a broken stick into a beautiful goal. After going viral with the stick fix, the 37-year-old Flames assistant equipment manager arrived at the Saddledome Friday morning a bashful celebrity of sorts. “Joel Hanley came up to me and said, ‘You’ve got more assists than I do this year,'" chuckled the popular dressing room assistant. It's a pretty unique accomplishment for a guy whose usual highlights involve skate sharpeners, laundry and equipment bags. Nemec had his stick slashed in half in his own zone Thursday against Minnesota, and while approaching the bench with speed, he contemplated a change when he spotted Dumaine holding out his backup. He grabbed it on the fly, kept going up ice and turned a two-on-one into a three-on-one. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images As the Toronto Maple Leafs continue to plummet down the standings, with Thursday’s 4-3 shootout loss to the Los Angeles Kings marking their eighth defeat in a row, it’s hard not to wonder whether head coach Jim Hiller could be relieved of his duties sooner rather than later. One person, however, that apparently isn’t worried about the coach’s job security, is Hiller himself. After Toronto’s general manager John Chayka expressed his belief in Hiller on Monday, Hiller spoke to reporters on Friday and addressed the rumors that his job could be in jeopardy. “Not something I think about too much,” Hiller said. “I appreciate that John did that. My job is to get the team to win games. We haven’t won enough, so I get them ready to win tomorrow.” Among other criticisms, Hiller’s handling of winger Gavin McKenna, the first-overall pick in the 2026 NHL Entry Draft, has come under scrutiny. The 18-year-old rookie did not receive a shift during Thursday’s 3-on-3 overtime period against the Kings. Hiller discussed his rationale behind keeping McKenna on the bench for overtime. “I think when we have some time where we’ll do some 3-on-3,” Hiller said. “We haven’t had a lot of practice time this year in getting preparation for the season. It’s a short season. But we’re going to do that. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources One of the game’s most respected players has earned a new title with one of the PWHL’s newest franchises. On Friday, the Vegas Vanguards announced that the team has named defender Erin Ambrose the first captain in franchise history. Forwards Hayley Scamurra and Tessa Janecke have been named alternates for the expansion team’s inaugural season. Ambrose was one of the foundational signings for the franchise in Sin City. She brings immediate legitimacy to the team and stability on the blue line. The Canadian National Team mainstay spent the first three seasons of the PWHL with the Montreal Victoire, helping the team win its first Walter Cup this past spring. This isn’t the first time Ambrose is in a leadership role in the PWHL. During her time with the Victoire, she was an alternate captain, supporting Marie-Philip Poulin . The Keswick, Ont. native will be seeking her first goal since the league’s first season with her new team, as Ambrose posted just six assists in 21 regular-season games last year. In 73 regular-season contests in her PWHL career, Ambrose has scored four goals and 37 points, with another five points in 16 playoff contests. Scamurra comes to Vegas with Ambrose from Montreal. She’s coming off the best season of her tenure in the league, scoring eight goals and 16 points during the regular season, adding another four points in the postseason. Janecke is thrust into the spotlight with the Vanguards. She was the team’s first-ever draft pick, taken third overall in the 2026 PWHL Draft in June. She enters the PWHL after a sensational career at Penn State, where she was a top-three finalist for the Patty Kazmaier Award in her senior season. Los Angeles rallied from a 3-0 deficit, with Kempe picking up an assist along the way, to force overtime. The 30-year-old proceeded to score the lone goal in the shootout, giving the Kings a hard-fought 4-3 win. This isn’t the first time Kempe has faced supplemental discipline in his NHL career. In January 2025, the Swedish winger was fined $5,000 for slew-footing Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid. Kempe has never been suspended by the NHL DoPS. The money from the fine goes to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Vilmer Salen Forsberg (Brandon Taylor OHL Images) Everyone knows goalies are the hardest to project. There’s one, Vilmer Salén Forsberg, who will probably appear at the top of every single list. Beyond that, though, you’re going to find plenty of variation. items.summary: The backbone, fortitude and discipline that allowed the Canucks to build a two-game win streak were wholly absent in Seattle.
items.body: SEATTLE — Winning streaks. So hard to build, so easy to blow. After waiting 23 games to construct their first two-game winning streak of the National Hockey League season, the Vancouver Canucks never gave themselves a chance here Thursday to count to three. Actually, goalie Leevi Merilainen gave the Canucks a chance, but he was about the only one. Teammates didn’t respond or rally around his brilliant performance through 28 minutes and eventually lost 5-1 to the Seattle Kraken. The backbone, fortitude and discipline that allowed the Canucks to respond to difficult stretches or untimely goals-against in their surprising wins this week against the Vegas Golden Knights and Utah Mammoth were wholly absent in Seattle. After getting outshot 24-5 in the opening period, the Canucks surrendered another nine shots in the first nine minutes of the second. The Kraken scored twice in 54 seconds, starting at the eight-minute mark, to pull ahead 3-1. And given the avalanche of shots and Kraken skaters bombarding Merilainen’s net, the Canucks never looked capable of coming back from two goals down. The Canucks have false-started in a pile of games this season, and posted absolute duds in a few. But even for a last-place team, their reversal in form from Las Vegas and Salt Lake City was surprising. “A little bit,” Canucks coach Manny Malhotra conceded. “Just in terms of how off we were and how badly we got outshot. (I was) expecting a better response. I think the guys had a much clearer understanding coming into tonight that we earned what we got in our previous two games just by the work ethic — the winning of puck battles, establishing a forecheck, those types of things. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images There’s a new head of the round table in Sin City, as winger Mark Stone is now the Vegas Golden Knights ‘ leader in career points. Stone achieved the milestone midway through Thursday’s 4-3 shootout loss to the Dallas Stars . The Golden Knights were on the power play down 2-0 at this point of the game, and after Jack Eichel passed the puck to Stone behind the net, the Vegas captain made a quick pass across the slot to Victor Olofsson, who did what he does best and buried it with a one-timer. That began a rally of three consecutive goals of Vegas to overcome the 2-0 deficit, only for Thomas Harley to tie the game in the final five minutes and eventually beat the Golden Knights in the shootout. With the assist, Stone gets the 418th point of his Golden Knights career, and puts him atop the franchise’s all-time scoring records. He surpasses Jonathan Marchessault, who had established the previous record of 417 points ever since the end of the 2023-24 season, his final season in Vegas before departing in free agency and signing with the Nashville Predators . However, Stone establishes the record in just 423 games, while Marchessault did so in 514 games with the franchise. This season, Stone has continued his established consistency on the scoresheet since joining the Golden Knights, as he has 11 goals and 11 assists for 22 points in 24 games . Stone isn’t entirely safe as the team’s all-time scoring leader though, as center William Karlsson is only five points behind the Golden Knights captain. items.title: Berkly Catton scores hat trick as Kraken beat Canucks
items.body: SEATTLE — Berkly Catton had his first NHL hat trick, Matty Beniers had a goal and an assist, and the Seattle Kraken snapped a three-game losing streak with a 5-1 win over the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday night. Brandon Montour had a pair of assists and Philipp Grubauer had 22 saves for the Kraken, playing their first game back in North America after losing a pair to the Carolina Hurricanes on Finland. Jake DeBrusk scored for the Canucks, who had won two in a row, while Leevi Merilainen made 38 saves. Catton scored a goal in each period starting with a power-play goal in the first. DeBrusk countered with a power-play goal to make it 1-1 after the first period. Catton and Beniers scored 54 seconds apart in the second to make it 3-1 Seattle after two periods, and Catton capped the hat trick with an empty-netter with 43 seconds remaining. He now has at least one point in his last seven home games.

items.summary: At age 36, Drew Doughty is ready for a pay cut. But he wants to go back to Cali in 2027-28. Luke Fox caught up with the longtime Kings defenceman about free agency and more.
items.body: TORONTO — Rare is the occasion when a hockey player openly floats a dollar figure that would likely convince him to sign a new deal with his hockey team. But Drew Doughty is nothing if not unique, and the impending unrestricted free agent has no designs on playing coy with the club he loves. As the newly minted captain of the Los Angeles Kings — the club that drafted him second overall more than 18 years ago — sits in a Scotiabank Arena visitors’ room stall, he considers fellow multi-Cup-winning superstars like Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin in Pittsburgh and the idea of sticking with one team till the very end. “I only want to wear one sweater. I want to live the rest of my life in L.A., even when I’m done playing. I mean, I’ve already lived half of my life in L.A. I’ve lived there for… this is my 19th year. So, I think it's amazing to be able to stay with one team. But I see where you're going with that,” says the ever-candid Doughty. “That's why, I mean, if they can sign me for, say, $4 to $6 million or something like that — with me still playing the most minutes on the team — I think that’s a hell of a deal for them.” Them is general manager Ken Holland and the L.A. brass, who announced prior to puck drop that they will take a wait-and-see approach with their outspoken, gap-toothed, universally beloved icon during 2026-27, the final season of No. 8’s eight-year, $88-million contract. items.title: Gauthier’s goal streak ends at 10 games as Ducks get shut out by Avalanche
items.body: DENVER — Brock Nelson had two goals and an assist as the Colorado Avalanche blanked Anaheim 4-0 on Thursday night, ending Cutter Gauthier 's goal-scoring streak at 10 games for the Ducks. Scott Wedgewood made 26 saves in his 13th career shutout and first this season. He became the first goaltender to keep Gauthier from scoring since Vancouver's Leevi Merilainen on Oct. 27. The 22-year-old left winger was the first NHL player with a goal in 10 consecutive games since Teemu Selanne set the Anaheim record with an 11-game run in 1997. Gauthier had four hat tricks during the streak, including Tuesday night in an 8-6 defeat at St. Louis. Gauthier also went without a point for the first time since Oct. 22 at New Jersey, stopping a 12-game streak. Devon Toews had a goal and an assist, and Nicolas Roy also scored for the Avalanche, who bounced back from a 4-1 loss Wednesday night at scuffling Utah. Martin Necas added two assists. Lukas Dostal stopped 24 shots for the Ducks, who have lost four of five since a five-game winning streak.

items.title: Mark Stone sets new Golden Knights all-time points record
items.body: Mark Stone stands alone on the Vegas Golden Knights ' all-time leaderboard. The team's long-time captain set a new franchise points record with an assist on Victor Olofsson's power-play goal in the second period of Thursday's game against the Dallas Stars. The assist gives Stone 418 points for his career, surpassing the previous record set by Jonathan Marchessault, who had 417 points in a Golden Knights uniform. Stone, a Winnipeg native, has scored 147 goals and 270 assists for Vegas after being traded from the Ottawa Senators at the 2019 trade deadline. So far this season, Stone has kept a pace of 21 points (11 goals, 10 assists) in 23 games played for the Golden Knights.

The players compete in front of hundreds of NHL scouts with an opportunity to enhance their standing ahead of the draft. Although the event is entering its third year, it has featured one top-10 NHL Draft pick from the NTDP. Forward Wyatt Cullen , who had a goal and an assist in the United States' 4-2 victory in Game 1 last season, was selected by the Nashville Predators with the No. 10 pick in the 2026 NHL Draft. Cullen became the sixth top-10 pick produced by the NTDP in the past five drafts. items.title: Rangers finding identity amid strong start to season
items.summary: GREENBURGH, N.Y. -- Mike Sullivan's rides to the rink have been far less stressful in his second season as the New York Rangers coach than they were in his first.
items.body: Playing physical, faster in Sullivan’s second year behind bench GREENBURGH, N.Y. -- Mike Sullivan's rides to the rink have been far less stressful in his second season as the New York Rangers coach than they were in his first. That happens when a coach is confident his team has an identity and will consistently play to it, as the Rangers have for a large enough percentage of their first 22 games this season. "When I drive to the rink, I feel fairly confident that I know the type of game that the players are going to put on the ice," Sullivan said. "Some nights are better than others but that's just part of it, that's just the human element of sports, but our intentions, our compete level, our mindset, things of that nature, are in the right place most nights, if not all. As a coach that's a good feeling when you're driving to the rink." Sullivan's rides were never easy last season, especially at home, where the Rangers turned Madison Square Garden into their own house of horrors in his first season in New York, winning 14 of 41 games, the No. 1 reason they were last in the Eastern Conference with 77 points. This season, the Rangers (13-8-1) have won nine of 11 home games, 13 of 22 overall, including three in a row and six of their past seven. They're third in the Metropolitan Division and in the middle of a five-day break before playing the Carolina Hurricanes at home Sunday. And they've done most of it without their best player, goalie Igor Shesterkin , who went down with a season-ending right knee injury in the sixth game of the season, at the Washington Capitals on Oct. 9. items.body: CALGARY - For nine lonely months, Jonathan Huberdeau wondered if he’d ever return to the game that’s given him everything. So when he stepped onto the ice for his first game since hip resurfacing surgery, his Calgary Flames teammates wanted him to know he wasn’t alone. Everything you need to know about how beloved Huberdeau is in the Flames organization was on full display Wednesday night at the Dome when the 33-year-old winger was warming up for his first AHL game with the Wranglers. A quick glance up along the glass allowed Huberdeau to spot Mikael Backlund , Ryan Strome and Joel Hanley, standing with their young children, alongside his own son. Given the early-morning skates, solo workouts, and the uncertainty of wondering if his hip would ever cooperate again, it was an awfully powerful moment. "It warms my heart, because that means they actually really care about each other - it's not lip service," said coach Ryan Huska, who was on hand with his coaching staff to witness the moment. "He really means a lot to them, and it goes the other way as well. It was cool to see, for sure. "There isn't a better team guy that you'd ever be around than Jonathan Huberdeau, and he's rubbed off in so many different ways to all of our players. When they see the struggles that he went through to get himself to the point to play, they're really proud of him, and they are in his corner 100 per cent." When Huberdeau looked up towards the owners’ suite, he saw members of what the coaches joke is his Boy Band: Matt Coronato, Morgan Frost, Joel Farabee, Zayne Parekh, as well as Matvei Gridin and Brennan Othmann. items.title: Lane Hutson leads Canadiens to gutsiest win of season
items.summary: The Hurricanes tried to push them. But Lane Hutson and the Canadiens didn’t just get up and push back, they pushed the Hurricanes over in a way they haven’t been able to in recent memory.
items.body: This was Lane Hutson as we’ve never seen him before — doubled over, gasping for the air that had been knocked out of him by the type of hit he’s so rarely been on the receiving end of since he jitterbugged his way into the NHL at the end of the 2023-24 season. Hutson was uncharacteristically lackadaisical, atypically unaware of Shayne Gostisbehere’s presence. He never saw it coming. But it was Gostisbehere and the Carolina Hurricanes who, in the end, were on the end of an unforeseen outcome. Because Hutson bounced back up from that second-period hit that left him winded and eventually took everyone’s breath away. First with a stunner of a tying goal late in the third period. And then with the winner that made it 2-1 Montreal Canadiens in overtime to cap their gutsiest performance of the season. “Everyone stepped up,” Hutson told reporters at Lenovo Center. That was right after Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis referred to it as a win that made them “better as a team.” It’s exactly what we were thinking with each passing minute of the game, as the Canadiens finally bore their teeth against this hungry pack of wolves. Oh sure, they beat the Hurricanes three times last regular season and once more at the start of the Eastern Conference Final last spring. But none of those games looked like this one, with the Canadiens pinching all the pressure points the Hurricanes typically have a firm grasp of. That they did it less than 24 hours after registering a bounce-back win against the red-hot Devils in New Jersey, that they did it missing several key players, and that they did it against a Hurricanes team that’s still sitting with the NHL’s best points percentage (.795) despite the loss, said everything about how much their character has grown since that lopsided playoff series.

I don't think they want me to go anywhere.” Doughty was named captain of the Kings on Sept. 16, taking the place of Anze Kopitar, who retired after last season. The 36-year-old defenseman, who was the No. 2 pick by the Kings at the 2008 NHL Draft, has played his entire career for Los Angeles and has 717 points (166 goals, 551 assists) in 1,298 games. The two-time Stanley Cup champion (2012, 2014) is in the final season of an eight-year, $88 million contract he signed with Los Angeles on July 1, 2018. He can become an unrestricted free agent this coming July 1. “It doesn't bother me,” Doughty said. “I haven’t thought about it at all. It (stinks) if you get injured or something, you start thinking, like the other day I blocked a shot and I thought ‘Oh, this isn't good for my next contract’ but I don't think about it. I don’t care.” Winner of the 2016 Norris Trophy voted as the best defenseman in the NHL, Doughty has also been a staple for Team Canada. He won Olympic gold for his country in 2010 and 2014, and helped Canada win the World Cup of Hockey 2016 and the Four Nations Face-Off in 2025. He was a member of Team Canada at the 2026 Winter Olympics, winning a silver medal. This season, he has eight points (one goal, seven assists) in 19 games. items.title: Two Oilers streaks snapped in stingy loss to Lightning
items.summary: Two Oilers streaks were put to bed in a stingy loss to the Lightning on Thursday. The defeat marked Edmonton’s first road regulation loss of the season, and the first game in which Connor McDavid was unable to crack the score sheet.
items.body: At some point, the Edmonton Oilers were going to lose a road game in regulation this season. And at some point, Connor McDavid was going to play a game in the 2026-27 season without picking up a point. Well, the Tampa Bay Lightning killed two birds with one stone Thursday, knocking Edmonton off by a 3-1 score and shutting out McDavid, snuffing both the Oilers' pursuits on one salty Florida night. “In the end, they were better than us and capitalized on their opportunities,” Oilers head coach Mike Babcock told reporters in Tampa. “I didn't think either team had a ton of opportunities here today.” This game was similar to Edmonton’s trip-opening, 1-0 win at Toronto. There was a bit more offence in this one, but it was two teams locking ‘er down for most of the night. “It was a pretty stingy game,” agreed Oilers defenceman Matias Ekholm. “They get a huge power-play goal to get the (1-0) lead, and the lead is so big in these types of games, since the other team has to open up a little bit. We weren't able to recover, really. “Give them credit; they played good. Their goalie (Andrei Vasilevskiy) was good. I thought we played okay, but I think we have another level." Edmonton is now 1-22-1 in the Lightning’s barn since the 2011-12 campaign. items.body: CALGARY — Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes extended their point streaks to 13 games on Thursday to lead the Minnesota Wild to a 4-1 victory over the Calgary Flames . Kaprizov and Matt Boldy each had a goal and two assists, while Hughes and Joel Eriksson Ek both had a goal and an assist for Minnesota (17-3-4), which has won five in a row and has points in 13 consecutive games (11-0-2). Its last regulation loss was a 2-1 setback to the Flames on Oct. 22. Earning the victory was Jesper Wallstedt, who made 22 saves to improve to 16-2-3. He leads the NHL in wins, four more than second place Pyotr Kochetkov. The Wild have also won nine straight on the road, equalling their second-longest streak in franchise history. The record is 12 set in 2014-15. Simon Nemec scored the lone goal for Calgary (10-12-1). Dustin Wolf had 18 stops for Calgary. He fell to 5-6-1. It didn't take long for Kaprizov to get on the scoresheet combining with Boldy to set up Eriksson Ek's deflection goal just 25 seconds into the game. At 8:09 of the first period, it was Hughes' turn to extend his point streak when he whipped a shot past Wolf from the blueline to make it 2-0. The 13-game point streaks for Kaprizov (eight goals, 18 assists) and Hughes (six goals, 15 assists) are the longest active streaks in the NHL with Connor McDavid's 23-game streak being snapped on Thursday. items.title: Wild’s Quinn Hughes exits in win over Flames
items.body: The Minnesota Wild picked up a 4-1 win over the Calgary Flames on Thursday, but it may have come at a price. Superstar defenceman Quinn Hughes exited late in the contest after he was on the receiving end of a hit from Flames forward Adam Klapka midway through the third period. Wild head coach John Hynes had no update on Hughes' status after the game, but he did confirm to reporters the defenceman was not removed by the concussion spotter. Hughes headed straight to the locker room after the hit and did not return for the remainder of the game. He made his presence felt before leaving, as he had a goal and an assist in 23:24 of ice time. Hughes' two points on Thursday bring his season totals to eight goals and 26 assists over the first 24 games of the season. The Wild also overtook the Oilers for the best record in the league by beating the Flames, as they now sit atop the overall standings with a 17-3-4 record. Minnesota's next game is against the Canucks on Saturday, and we will have to wait and see if Hughes is back to take on his former team in Vancouver for a second time this season.

items.body: Even though the Toronto Maple Leafs lost their eighth straight contest on Thursday, they don't need to worry about the health of their captain. Auston Matthews took an awkward fall at the end of the Maple Leafs' 4-3 shootout loss to the Los Angeles Kings and was in visible discomfort as the buzzer sounded. The once 69-goal scorer collided with Quinton Byfield trying to enter the zone and took a tumble onto the ice. He was grabbing his side while grimacing as he slowly made his way to the bench before the shootout. Matthews still managed to take the Maple Leafs' first shootout attempt following the injury scare. Following the game, Matthews said he just "felt kind of weird" after the collision, but "after a couple of minutes it was fine." Matthews has 13 goals and 19 assists for 32 points through 24 games this season. items.body: WASHINGTON — Rasmus Dahlin and Beck Malenstyn scored 25 seconds apart in the first period to chase Logan Thompson, and the Buffalo Sabres sent Washington to its fourth straight loss, beating the Capitals 6-3 on Thursday night. Jack Quinn scored twice — once into an empty net — and Zach Benson and Tage Thompson also scored for the Sabres. Buffalo converted on five of its 13 shots in the first two periods. Alex Tuch, Ryan Leonard and Boone Jenner scored Washington, which has fallen to .500 after entering the season with lofty expectations. Alex Ovechkin broke a tie with longtime teammate Nicklas Backstrom for Washington's career lead in assists with his 763rd. The Capitals have allowed at least five goals in four straight games and six of their last eight. On Wednesday it took them only two periods to do so. Thompson allowed three goals on five shots before being yanked in favour of Charlie Lindgren. It was the second time in his last six starts Thompson was pulled early. After Quinn opened the scoring, Dahlin entered the zone on a power play, and when Thompson overplayed him a bit to the near post, the Buffalo defenceman swooped behind the net and wrapped the puck into the vacated other side. items.title: Connor McDavid’s season-opening point streak ends at 23 games
items.body: For the first time this season, Connor McDavid failed to find the scoresheet. McDavid had his 23-game point streak come to an end as the Edmonton Oilers lost to the Tampa Bay Lightning 3-1 on Thursday. The 23-game tear was the longest point streak of McDavid's career, and tied for the fourth-longest to open a season in NHL history. Wayne Gretzky holds the record for the longest season-opening point streak at 51 games, which he set in the 1983-84 season. McDavid will finish his epic run with a staggering 13 goals and 42 assists for a league-leading 55 points. Thursday's loss to the Lightning also snapped a six-game Oilers win streak. Lightning goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy came within 1:39 of recording his first shutout of the season. Nikita Kucherov, John Carlson and Ilya Mikheyev scored for Tampa Bay, which improved to 10-1 at home. Devon Levi stopped 17 shots for Edmonton, and Shakir Mukhamadullin scored for the Oilers. Edmonton lost for the first time in regulation on the road this season, falling to 10-1-1. Following a scoreless first, the Lightning broke the ice on their second power play chance of the game. Brayden Point slipped a pass from the corner down low to Jake Guentzel who swung behind the net and zipped a pass to Carlson in the middle slot for a one-timer at 13:29. Mikheyev gave Tampa Bay a 2-0 lead at 10:46 of the third period. Kucherov made it 3-0 on a breakaway chance at 14:29. The Lightning placed Brandon Hagel on injured reserve earlier on Thursday.

Penguins reporter Katie Florio had a new hairstyle for Thursday's game - lavender streaks added to her dark locks - to show solidarity with all those involved with the fight against cancer. It was Hockey Fights Cancer night in Pittsburgh and Florio used her airtime to share her personal story. At 15 years old she was diagnosed with a brain tumor. It affected not only her teenage self, but her entire family. "No warnings, no nothing, it came out of absolutely nowhere," Florio said. "In the blink of an eye, my family's life was turned upside down." Florio went on to thank everyone who supported her and her doctors at Duke Children's Hospital, sharing a picture with her pediatric neurosurgeon, Dr. Fuchs. "I can now sit here today and say I'm here, I'm healthy, I beat it and I am so, so thankful for that," she said. "That experience taught me that the diagnosis doesn't just affect the person it's given to. It impacts entire families. It changes lives and it puts so much into perspective. Without the two-time Norris winner the Avs have leaned on impressive undrafted right-hander Sam Malinski . Beckman, 25, will have the opportunity to play in his first NHL contest since April 2024 as a member of the Wild. Drafted by Minnesota in the third round seven years ago, the winger broke the 100-point mark in his last full junior season as a Spokane Chief, generating some hype with his high end shot and making a quick Wild debut at age 20. Suiting up for 22 more games over the years with three assists, at this point he has made most of his impact in the AHL. Proving himself as a reliable scorer for the Iowa Wild with defensive shortcomings, not uncommon for non-prospects who light up the AHL, the Saskatoon native Beckman made stops with the Utica Comets and Bridgeport Islanders. He put together a 30-goal campaign last season for the New York farm club prior to catching on as part of the Avalanche organization. items.body: Register Login Ducks Recall Stian Solberg By Bradley Keith | at November 19, 2026 7:00 pm Ahead of tonight’s matchup in Colorado the Ducks announced that standout prospect Stian Solberg has been recalled from AHL San Diego. The news came after Travis Mitchell successfully passed through waivers . Solberg, a defenseman, was one of Anaheim’s two first round choices in the 2024 draft (23rd overall) after they snagged Beckett Sennecke twenty picks prior. The Norwegian stands at 6’2″ and is your typical physical presence with solid mobility and the ability to chip in offensively. Coming out of Norway, the lefty skated in 47 SHL games in 2024-25 before coming over, teammates with Damian Clara on Färjestad BK. Last year in his first full North American campaign the 20-year-old racked up 102 penalty minutes in 71 games to go along with 24 points. He was able to find the back of the net consistently for a player not always known for offense, leading AHL rookie defenders in goals (12). This season that offense has shown some nice growth with 11 points in just his first 17 appearances.
